description.value: The study investigated how directing attention to the healthiness or tastiness of healthy food affects food choice and BOLD activity, including whether BMI moderates these neural responses.

spans.text: Here, we investigate whether brain activity in those areas involved in self-control may increase significantly when individuals with a high body-mass index (BMI) focus their attention on the taste rather than on the health benefits related to healthy food choices.

value: Drawing attention to healthy food would lead to significantly increased activity in those brain areas that are associated with self-control and reward value during healthy food choices, regardless of whether attention is paid to the healthiness or tastiness of food, and help people to make healthy food choices.
For higher BMI individuals, focusing on the healthiness decreases the brain activity in these brain areas.
Whereas focusing on the tastiness increases their brain activity in these brain areas.

description.value: An observational, single-group fMRI study of 23 participants, with one exclusion for excessive motion, involving repeated food-choice conditions.

spans.text: the participants were not explicitly asked to control themselves

name.value: BMI negatively correlated with activation during healthy food choice in the no diet condition

definition.value: negative correlation between BMI and activation during healthy food choice in the no diet condition

value: A significant negative correlation between BMI and cortical responses was documented in the left insula and the left inferior frontal operculum.
Such findings suggest that highlighting healthiness in food communications may help to render healthy food less appetizing for high BMI individuals.

name.value: BMI negatively correlated with activation during healthy food choice in the healthy diet condition

definition.value: negative correlation between BMI and cortical responses during healthy food choice in the healthy diet condition compared with the no diet condition

value: An inverse relationship between BMI and the activity of the OFC/vmPFC is observed.
This suggests that the choice of healthy food may be less valued amongst those individuals with a higher BMI.

name.value: BMI positively correlated with activation during healthy food choice in the tasty diet condition

definition.value: positive correlation between BMI and cortical responses during healthy food choice in the tasty diet condition compared with the no diet condition

value: A significant positive correlation between BMI and cortical responses was observed in the insula, the left OFC, the anterior cingulate cortex, the right IFG, and several other regions.
These results support previous work suggesting that obese individuals are more sensitive to the expected pleasure of consumption as compared to non-obese individuals.
